# llms.txt — AI-first entry point for RACS
# Adopted per nsolland/Racs#64 / nsolland/Index#338
# This file is the canonical machine-readable orientation for AI agents.
# Human-readable overview lives in README.md; this file is for machine interpretation first.

# Stable identity
- stable_id: valo.racs
- canonical_name: RACS
- full_name: Runtime Agent Control Standard
- purpose: Neutral, model-agnostic protocol for representing, evaluating, authorizing, executing, and evidencing AI-mediated actions.
- public_url: https://github.com/nsolland/Racs
- version: 0.2
- normative_status: normative
- maturity: implemented

# What RACS owns (contract boundary)
- owns: canonical receipt and evidence contract
- owns: action envelope schema
- owns: authority / policy / evidence context schemas
- owns: governance evaluation, determination, clearance schemas
- does_not_own: execution authority grant (REHT owns admissibility)
- does_not_own: action execution (Core owns execution)
- does_not_own: evidence evaluation (VAIG owns evaluation)

# Key invariants
- Platform-local receipt objects MUST map to RACS, not become competing standards.
- Receipts link proposal, evaluation, clearance, execution, and outcome.
- Evidence integrity, provenance, and immutable linkage are contract concerns.
- RACS records decisions and effects; it does NOT grant clearance or execute actions.

# Repository map (normative vs informative)
- spec/ : PUBLIC, NORMATIVE — protocol schemas and semantics
- reference/ : PUBLIC, INFORMATIVE — example implementations (python, rust, typescript)
- examples/ : PUBLIC, INFORMATIVE — domain action examples
- test-vectors/ : PUBLIC, INFORMATIVE — compliance and runtime vectors
- validators/ : PUBLIC, INFORMATIVE — compliance checkers
- .github/workflows/ : PUBLIC, INFORMATIVE — CI validation

# Start here for agents
- Read first: spec/action-envelope.yaml (core action message format)
- Contract lock: reference/bindings/v0.2 (typed bindings, canonicalization, runtime conformance)
- Governance: nsolland/Index (REHT-101..REHT-105 requirement identifiers)
- REHT-104: every clearance decision MUST issue a receipt. Map RACS receipt fields to REHT-104 without redefining REHT admissibility.

# Related repositories (stable identifiers)
- valo.reht : consumes-admissibility (https://github.com/nsolland/Index)
- valo.vaig : consumes-evaluation (https://github.com/nsolland/Index)
- valo.core : consumes-execution (https://github.com/nsolland/Index)
- baro : consumes-evidence (https://github.com/nsolland/Index)

# Non-claims
- RACS is a protocol specification, not a runtime.
- RACS does not grant clearance or execute actions.
- RACS does not define domain-specific policy; policy is data.
- RACS is vendor-neutral; external proof formats may be mapped but not privileged as governance authority.
